purpose: Frozen blind held-out answer-quality set. Measure once per system; never use these cases, gold claims, passages, or measurements for tuning. Curated directly from the corpus without running any answer system.

cases.query: What personal qualities did Buffett want in the people running a potential stock investment in 1977?

gold_claims.claim: The people running the business should be honest and competent.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1977_p0028: criterion (3) explicitly calls for honest and competent people operating the business.

cases.query: Why did Berkshire borrow money in 1980 even though it had no pressing need for financing?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire wanted financial firepower for opportunities when credit was unavailable.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1980_p0076: it denies immediate financing needs and says attractive opportunities may arise when credit is extremely expensive or unavailable, requiring financial firepower.

cases.query: Did Buffett think gaining control justified paying twice as much per share in his 1981 hypothetical acquisition example?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire would rather buy 10% at X per share than 100% at 2X per share.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1981_p0006: its first paragraph explicitly prefers 10% of Wonderful Business T at X per share to 100% at 2X, regardless of immediately reportable earnings.

cases.query: In Buffett's 1986 discussion of accounting, who is responsible for judging a business rather than merely recording its transactions?

gold_claims.claim: The evaluation job falls to investors and managers.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1986_p0150: it assigns recording to accountants and says the evaluation job falls to investors and managers.

cases.query: When investees kept earnings that Berkshire's accounts omitted, what did Buffett say mattered most in 1990?

gold_claims.claim: Ownership and subsequent utilization of those earnings are all-important.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1990_p0019: for forgotten-but-not-gone earnings, it explicitly contrasts unimportant accounting with all-important ownership and subsequent utilization.

cases.query: How did Buffett weigh a higher but uneven return against a lower steady return when discussing catastrophe insurance in 1996?

gold_claims.claim: Charlie and Buffett preferred a lumpy 15% over time to a smooth 12%.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1996_p0036: the super-cat paragraph expressly says Charlie and Buffett would rather earn a lumpy 15% over time than a smooth 12%.

cases.query: What drawback did Buffett see in using stock options to motivate executives in his 1998 discussion?

gold_claims.claim: Options are often inefficient as motivators.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1998_p0069: despite acknowledging properly structured options can be appropriate, its first paragraph describes them more often as inefficient as motivators.

cases.query: Beyond independence, what did Buffett regard as the hardest-to-find qualification for a board director in 2003?

gold_claims.claim: Business savvy was the rarest of the director qualities.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2003_p0054: after listing business savvy, shareholder orientation and genuine interest, it explicitly calls business savvy the rarest quality.

cases.query: What limits did Buffett put on monetary and fiscal stimulus as a remedy for the housing slump in his 2011 letter?

gold_claims.claim: Monetary and fiscal policies do not create households or eliminate excess housing units.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2011_p0026: it says wise monetary and fiscal policies temper recessions but do not create households or eliminate excess housing units.

cases.query: In 2023, what ability to reinvest made a business especially appealing to Berkshire?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire favors an enterprise that can deploy additional capital at high returns in the future.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2023_p0014: its first sentence identifies the favored rare enterprise as one able to deploy additional capital at high future returns.

cases.query: How did Buffett assess SAFECO's approach to reserving for losses in the 1978 letter?

gold_claims.claim: SAFECO's loss reserving was conservative.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1978_p0039: the SAFECO paragraph explicitly describes its loss reserving as conservative.

cases.query: Was buying Waumbec Mills cheaply a success in Buffett's 1979 account?

gold_claims.claim: The purchase of Waumbec Mills was a mistake.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1979_p0024: after calling the Waumbec purchase an extraordinary statistical bargain below working capital, Buffett explicitly says the purchase was a mistake.

cases.query: How did Nebraska Furniture Mart's single location compare with the rest of Omaha's home-furnishing sellers in 1983?

gold_claims.claim: That single store sold more furniture, carpets, and appliances than all Omaha competitors combined.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1983_p0017: its final sentence says NFM's single store sold more furniture, carpets and appliances than all Omaha competitors combined.

cases.query: Who took charge of Star Furniture in 1962, according to the history Buffett recounted in 1997?

gold_claims.claim: Melvyn and his sister Shirley Toomin took over in 1962.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1997_p0072: its first sentence identifies Melvyn and his sister Shirley Toomin as taking over Star in 1962.

cases.query: Why did R. C. Willey keep its stores shut on Sundays, as Buffett explained in 1999?

gold_claims.claim: R. C. Willey's stores were closed on Sunday because Bill and most managers were Mormons.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1999_p0016, and 1999_p0017 as continuation context: 1999_p0016 itself says Bill and most managers are Mormons and for that reason the stores have never operated on Sunday. Only 1999_p0016 supplies the claim.

cases.query: What did Berkshire pay for Justin Industries in the deal described in the 2000 letter, and was the payment in cash?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire bought Justin for $570 million in cash.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2000_p0024: after the Fort Worth meeting with John Roach and John Justin, it explicitly records buying Justin for $570 million in cash.

cases.query: Which two British electricity distributors were part of MidAmerican's operations in the 2008 letter?

gold_claims.claim: Yorkshire Electricity and Northern Electric were MidAmerican's British electricity distributors.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2008_p0028: item (1) names Yorkshire Electricity and Northern Electric and identifies their joint position as the U.K.'s third largest distributor.

cases.query: Who was leading Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance when Buffett introduced the new operation in 2013?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance was led by Peter Eastwood.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2013_p0046: it expands BHSI as Berkshire Hathaway Specialty Insurance and directly says BHSI is led by Peter Eastwood.

cases.query: How many Berkshire shares did Buffett regret issuing to acquire General Re in his 2016 review of the deal?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire issued 272,200 shares to buy General Re.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2016_p0018: Buffett calls issuing 272,200 Berkshire shares to buy General Re a terrible mistake. This is a retrospective in the 2016 letter, not a claim that the purchase happened in 2016.

cases.query: What stake in Nebraska Furniture Mart did Berkshire purchase, and what check did Mrs. B receive, as recalled in 1984?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire purchased 90% of NFM.
Mrs. B received a check for $55 million.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1984_p0034: its first paragraph explicitly gives the 90% NFM purchase and the check to Mrs. B for $55 million. The question dates the account, not the acquisition.

cases.query: How many charities received distributions through Berkshire's shareholder-directed giving scheme in 1985?

gold_claims.claim: There were 1,724 charities receiving contributions.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1985_p0143: its clean opening paragraph identifies 1,724 charities as recipients. A later duplicated continuation line is outside the evidence used.

cases.query: In 1988, how much profit did Buffett say Berkshire would need over the coming decade to achieve a 15% annual return?

gold_claims.claim: A 15% annual return over the next decade required profits of $10.3 billion.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1988_p0003: it says a 15% return for the next decade demands $10.3 billion of profits. This is a forward-looking requirement, not realized profits.

cases.query: What acquisition price does the 1994 letter give for Scott Fetzer?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire paid $315.2 million for Scott Fetzer.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 1994_p0017: the second paragraph directly states the $315.2 million purchase price. The first paragraph dates the acquisition to the beginning of 1986, distinct from the letter year.

cases.query: How much float was Berkshire holding from GEICO in the 2001 account?

gold_claims.claim: GEICO's float was $4.25 billion.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete texts of 2001_p0060 and 2001_p0061: the GEICO paragraph begins in 2001_p0060, and the continuation in 2001_p0061 explicitly states $4.25 billion in float. Claim-level citation is assigned to 2001_p0061 where both required terms occur.

cases.query: About how much gas did the Kern River pipeline move each day before the expansion discussed in 2002?

gold_claims.claim: Kern River moved about 900 million cubic feet of gas a day.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2002_p0024: after identifying Kern River, it gives current throughput of about 900 million cubic feet daily before the expansion expected to double it.

cases.query: What was Berkshire's cash-plus-Treasury-bill balance at the end of 2017?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire held $116.0 billion in cash and U.S. Treasury Bills at yearend.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2017_p0047: it explicitly states yearend cash and U.S. Treasury Bills of $116.0 billion; the $86.4 billion comparison is for yearend 2016, not the requested balance.

cases.query: How large was the write-down that Buffett tied mainly to overpaying for Precision Castparts in his 2020 letter?

gold_claims.claim: The write-down was $11 billion.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2020_p0020: its opening calls the GAAP write-down $11 billion and attributes it almost entirely to paying too much for PCC in 2016. The question concerns the 2020 charge, not the purchase year.

cases.query: What improvement in Berkshire's insurance combined ratio is shown by the 1984 and 1985 letters? Give the ratio for each year.

gold_claims.claim: The combined ratio in 1984 was 134.
The combined ratio in 1985 was 111.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete texts of 1984_p0057 and 1985_p0104: the former reports a combined ratio of 134 in 1984; the latter explicitly reports its improvement to 111 in 1985. Each year has a separate claim-level passage assignment.

cases.query: How did the earnings hurdle for acquisition candidates differ between Berkshire's 1983 and 2014 criteria? Include the tax basis and the later exception.

gold_claims.claim: The earlier hurdle was at least $5 million of after-tax earnings.
The later hurdle was at least $75 million of pre-tax earnings.
The later hurdle had an exception for a business that would fit into one of the existing units.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete texts of 1983_p0095 and 2014_p0136: item (1) in each directly states its earnings hurdle. The earlier basis is after-tax; the later is pre-tax and explicitly excepts businesses fitting an existing unit. No like-for-like earnings multiple is inferred.

cases.query: What market-share figures did NetJets report in the 2002 and 2003 letters, and what sales or aircraft-value measure accompanied each figure?

gold_claims.claim: NetJets' industry share in 2002 was 75%.
The earlier comparison valued the planes clients purchased or leased.
The later figure was 70% of net sales measured by value.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete texts of 2002_p0063 and 2003_p0110: the former gives 75% industry share based on the value of purchased or leased planes; the latter gives 70% of net sales measured by value. The question explicitly asks both definitions rather than inferring a like-for-like market-share decline.

cases.query: How did Berkshire's relationship with GEICO change between the ownership position described in 1986 and the takeover recalled in 2016?

gold_claims.claim: GEICO was 41% owned by Berkshire in the earlier account.
The GEICO purchase turned the holding into a wholly-owned operating business.
Berkshire acquired the remaining half at the beginning of 1996.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete texts of 1986_p0070 and 2016_p0017: the first identifies Berkshire's 41% GEICO ownership; the latter retrospectively dates acquiring the remaining half to the beginning of 1996 and calls the result a wholly-owned operating business. The takeover is not dated to 2016.

cases.query: What purchase prices did Buffett give for Berkshire's first used corporate jet in the 1986 letter and its replacement in the 1989 letter?

gold_claims.claim: The earlier used plane was bought for $850,000.
The replacement used jet cost $6.7 million.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete texts of 1986_p0120 and 1989_p0146: the former gives $850,000 for its used plane; the latter states that this jet was sold and another used jet bought for $6.7 million. Letter years label the accounts, not an inferred exact purchase date.

cases.query: At what price per dollar of receivables did they unload that troubled portfolio?

history.content: Let's discuss the unsuccessful GEICO credit-card venture covered in Berkshire's 2009 letter.
Which detail of that venture would you like to examine?

gold_claims.claim: The troubled portfolio was sold for 55¢ on the dollar.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2009_p0042: its credit-card paragraph explicitly says the troubled receivables portfolio was sold for 55¢ on the dollar. History supplies the venture and letter year, but no sale-price fact.

cases.query: What ownership stake in that holding company did Berkshire agree to buy?

history.content: Tell me about the proposed Heinz investment described in Berkshire's 2012 letter.
Which aspect of the proposed investment interests you?

gold_claims.claim: Berkshire agreed to buy 50% of the holding company.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2012_p0016: its opening says Berkshire agreed in February to buy 50% of a holding company owning all of H. J. Heinz. The question identifies the letter, not the calendar year of the February announcement. History contains no ownership percentage.

cases.query: Which investment manager first brought that company to Buffett's attention?

history.content: Let's look at the Precision Castparts acquisition discussed in Berkshire's 2015 letter.
Which part of the acquisition would you like to explore?

gold_claims.claim: Todd Combs brought the company to Buffett's attention.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2015_p0022: its personal thank-you credits Todd Combs with bringing the PCC company to Buffett's attention and educating him about it. History identifies only the acquisition and letter, not the manager.

cases.query: When did Berkshire first start buying that group of five companies?

history.content: Let's discuss Berkshire's Japanese trading-company investments in the 2024 letter.
Which part of those investments would you like to examine?

gold_claims.claim: The first purchases involving the five companies were in July 2019.

cases.verification_note: Opened the complete text of 2024_p0041: its first sentence dates the first purchases involving the five to July 2019. Opened neighboring 2024_p0040 and 2024_p0042 for referent context only, not as gold or relevant evidence; neither supplies the scored date. History contains no purchase date.
